adds.title: LGBTQ rights in Turkey - Wikipedia
adds.summary: Wikipedia's Turkey country overview dates the national framework every province, including Erzurum, sits under: homosexuality has been decriminalised since the Ottoman penal code of 1858, and transgender people have been able to change their legal gender since 1988 (gender-reassignment surgery legal since 1988). Same-sex marriage, civil unions and joint adoption are not recognised, LGBTQ people are barred from openly serving in the military, and Turkey has no comprehensive national law banning discrimination on grounds of sexual orientation or gender identity; a court case to close Lambda Istanbul was overruled by the Constitutional Court, keeping the association open. Pride events have been banned in Istanbul and other cities in most years since 2015, with police using tear gas, water cannons and mass detentions against participants, and ILGA-Europe's 2026 Rainbow Europe ranking placed Turkey 47th out of 49 countries. The page carries no Erzurum-specific content, but under the lane spec a national-framework document stays on a province record when that framework is what the visitor stands under and no province-specific source covers the point.
